thread:
jamie: quick question — for NDJSON exports, are we comfortable shipping full actor IDs by default? customers want a stable 'who' but legal wants minimal PII :thinking:
neha: prefer hashed IDs in exports + a mapping option behind a gated flag. reduces PII risk and still lets customers join events to their internal ids if they opt in
omar: what about telemetry? if we hash, we lose ability to correlate with internal tracing unless we keep a mapping in our infra (which is sensitive)
liz: can we do deterministic salted-hash + per-tenant salt that we rotate? then exports show actor_hash and console can resolve when tenant has enabled mapping. rotation policy needs thought
jamie: example config I was thinking for export API:
```
POST /exports
{ "format":"ndjson", "fields":["ts","action","actor_hash"], "actor_mode":"hashed", "salt_version": "v1" }
```
no mapping unless tenant opts in and signs TOU
neha: +1 but we need a retention policy for the mapping table if tenant opts in. product asked for 90 days default then archive
sre-bot: note: exporting actor mappings to S3 will hit our outbound egress quota for some customers — file chunking recommended :warning:
kai-prod: product perspective — customers (esp. security teams) expect 'who did X' to be actionable. If we bury identity behind a gated mapping, UX needs a clear banner and API reason codes. Also, legal teams may ask for subpoena workflows
omar: operationally we should also consider an export-only signing flow. If mapping exists, export includes a signed proof link to fetch full actor details (requires auth). That way long-lived NDJSON stays PII-lite
liz: UX: console export modal should offer two modes: "PII-minimal" (actor_hash) and "Full (request mapping)". Show telemetry that chooses default based on tenant compliance profile
jamie: edge-case: rollback events where actor is a service account. We probably want to show service-account aliases even in hashed mode. Can add field actor_type to help parsers
neha: implementation note: use HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-specific key stored in KMS. Pseudocode:
```
actor_hash = hmac(kms_key_for_tenant, actor_id)
```
so we can rotate key by re-signing new events and keep previous salt/version for lookups
kai-prod: if we HMAC, we can guarantee non-reversibility (good). Product ok with mapping when tenant explicitly enables it and accepts responsibility
omar: followups: 1) quota impact for on-demand mapping resolution endpoint (if console hits it live), 2) telemetry tags for export type so billing/ops can track extra cost
jamie: for rollout plan: default export behavior -> actor_hash; gate for mapping via tenant feature-flag; announce in console and changelog; 30-day opt-in period for existing customers
neha: +1. I'll open a PR for the export shape (ndjson example + actor_mode enum). Also adding an integration test for sampling and chunked uploads
liz: can someone mockup the modal copy? I can wire it into the console if we have copy by EOD
omar: I'll add a rate-limit to /actor-resolve and emit a metric export.actor_resolve.latency and .rate_limited_count
sre-bot: deploy queued: infra/export-service:v2 -> canary on prod tomorrow 03:00 UTC
jamie: thanks all. capturing decisions: hashed-by-default, HMAC per-tenant key, opt-in mapping behind flag, export modal with explicit consent, signed fetch for full mapping. I'll add to the export RFC and link here
neha: tiny nit — document how we surface reason codes in export webhook failures (401 vs 403 vs 429). Otherwise 👍
jamie: agreed, will add. tagging @legal in the RFC review once draft done :eyes:
kai-prod: thanks — product will review the modal and compliance copy. :thumbsup:
